dataset.name: Bulk density, grain size, carbon content and isotopes, and nitrogen content of floodplain sediment along the Koyukuk River, Alaska collected in Summer 2018.
description: The dataset is comprised of grain size, bulk density, carbon and nitrogen content, stable carbon isotopes, and radiocarbon content of soils sampled on the floodplain of the Koyukuk River near Huslia, AK. This dataset was collected to characterize sediment properties and floodplain organic carbon stocks in the discontinuous permafrost floodplain of the Koyukuk River. The data help quantify the flux and storage of sediment and carbon between the Koyukuk River and the surrounding floodplain as the river migrates laterally. The samples were collected in June 27 - July 9, 2018. The soil samples come from a total of 24 locations and were sampled in the upper 490 cm of the river cutbanks, point bars, and floodplain. Samples were analyzed for bulk density, full particle size distribution, nitrogen content and carbon content and isotopes, though not all samples were included in each analysis. An additional 10 samples of floodplain woody debris were measured for radiocarbon content. Data, detailed methods, analyses, and interpretations were previously published at:

Douglas, M. M., Lingappa, U. F., Lamb, M. P., Rowland, J. C., West, A. J., Li, G., et al. (2021). Impact of river channel lateral migration on microbial communities across a discontinuous permafrost floodplain. Applied and Environmental Microbiology, 87(20), AEM.01339-21. https://doi.org/10.1128/AEM.01339-21

Douglas, M. M., Li, G. K., Fischer, W. W., Rowland, J. C., Kemeny, P. C., West, A. J., et al. (2022). Organic carbon burial by river meandering partially offsets bank erosion carbon fluxes in a discontinuous permafrost floodplain. Earth Surface Dynamics, 10(3), 421–435. https://doi.org/10.5194/esurf-10-421-2022
The dataset is comprised of a total of three separate data files based on the sample type and analysis, including a file that lists the sample locations, permafrost presence, and geomorphic landform.

File: Koyukuk_River_Floodplain_Sample_Sites.csv
Summary of sample site characteristics and location.
Sample site = Name of sampling locations
Landform = Geomorphic landform relative to the river (cutbank/floodplain/point bar)
Latitude = Sampling location latitude in degrees
Longitude = Sampling location longitude in degrees
Frozen ground type = permafrost/non-permafrost. Permafrost locations are where we observed ice-cemented sediment and cryotextures indicative of permafrost. We did not observe ice-cemented sediment at locations classified as non-permafrost.

File: Koyukuk_River_Floodplain_Grain_Size_Distributions.csv
Complete grain size distributions of sediment samples after carbonate and organics removal measured 3x and averaged using laser diffraction.
Sample Name = sediment sample name in format “KY18-[Site]-[Depth below surface in cm]”
D10 (µm) = 10th percentile grain size measured in units of micrometers
D50 (µm) = median grain size/50th percentile measured in units of micrometers
D90 (µm) = 90th percentile grain size measured in units of micrometers
Remaining columns contain the probability distribution of grain size in 93 logarithmically spaced bins in units of micrometers. Column headers are in format [X]µm-[X]µm.

File: Koyukuk_River_Floodplain_Soil_Geochemistry.csv
Sample Name = sediment or woody debris sample name in format “KY18-[Site]-[Depth below surface in cm]”
Sample Site = sample site described in file Koyukuk_River_Floodplain_Sample_Sites.csv
Depth (cm) = depth below ground surface in centimeters
D50 (mm) = median sediment grain size measured using laser diffraction in millimeters
Stratigraphic Unit = stratigraphic grouping designated in the field by grain size and type of organic material as silt, sand, peat, topsoil, or woody debris
Water Content (wt%) = water content in weight percentage measured as (mass of sediment sample – mass of oven-dried sediment) x 100 / mass of sediment sample
Bulk Density (kg/m3) =
d13C (‰) = organic carbon stable isotope ratio measured using an isotope ratio mass spectrometer (IRMS) and reported relative to VPDB in units of per mille
TOC (dry wt%) = sediment total organic carbon content in weight percentage measured using an isotope ratio mass spectrometer (IRMS)
TN (dry wt%) = total nitrogen content in weight percentage measured using an isotope ratio mass spectrometer (IRMS)
Mass Ratio of TOC:TN = kg TOC per kg TN in sediment, dimensionless ratio
Fraction Modern = radiocarbon fraction modern for samples, measured using accelerator mass spectrometry at WHOI NOSAMS
Radiocarbon Age (BP) = uncalibrated radiocarbon ages, measured using accelerator mass spectrometry at WHOI NOSAMS
WHOI TOC (dry wt%) = sediment total organic carbon content measured at WHOI NOSAMS in the course of radiocarbon measurements
WHOI d13C (‰) = organic carbon stable isotope ratio measured at WHOI NOSAMS and reported relative to VPDB in units of per mille
Cap Delta 14C = the difference between sample radiocarbon activity reported relative to 1950 and sample activity corrected for age and δ13C, measured at WHOI NOSAMS. Measurements of the same sample made at different times will give the same Δ14C values.
